root_cause.text: The NCSI receive path mishandled skb ownership by returning directly from ncsi_aen_handler() and ncsi_rcv_rsp() on validation/lookup failures without freeing the received sk_buff in those error paths.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes early `return -ENOENT`/`return -ENODEV` sites to set `ret` and jump to cleanup (`goto out` in `ncsi_aen_handler()` and `goto err_free_skb` in `ncsi_rcv_rsp()`), and adds `kfree_skb(skb)` in `err_free_skb`, while the CVE/commit message explicitly says invalid AEN packets and failures to resolve the NCSI device, response handler, or request left the skb unfreed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Route the invalid-AEN error path through the common exit block so cleanup/finalization still runs before returning `-ENOENT`.
intent_record.what: The direct `return -ENOENT;` in the `if (!nah)` branch of `ncsi_aen_handler()` was replaced with assigning `ret = -ENOENT;` followed by `goto out;`.
intent_record.how: Instead of exiting the function immediately when an invalid AEN handler is missing, the code now routes execution through the common `out` path, ensuring any cleanup or finalization performed there still occurs while preserving the same error code.

intent_record.intent_summary: Route the missing-device error case through the skb cleanup path to avoid leaking the received buffer.
intent_record.what: The early return on a missing NCSI device private structure was replaced with setting ret to -ENODEV and jumping to the existing err_free_skb error path via goto err_free_skb.
intent_record.how: When ndp is not found, the function now follows the common cleanup path instead of returning immediately, ensuring the received skb is freed before exiting and preventing a resource leak on this error path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Route the unrecognized-packet error case through the common cleanup path so the skb is freed before returning -ENOENT.
intent_record.what: The direct `return -ENOENT;` in the `if (!nrh)` branch of `ncsi_rcv_rsp()` was replaced with assigning `ret = -ENOENT;` followed by `goto err_free_skb;`.
intent_record.how: When an unrecognized packet is received, the function now follows the shared error-handling path instead of returning immediately, ensuring the socket buffer is freed before exiting and preventing a resource leak.

intent_record.intent_summary: Route the unused-request error through the common cleanup path so the skb is freed before returning `-ENODEV`.
intent_record.what: The direct `return -ENODEV;` inside the `if (!nr->used)` branch was replaced with `ret = -ENODEV;` followed by `goto err_free_skb;`.
intent_record.how: Instead of exiting the function immediately when the request slot is unused, execution now jumps to the shared error-handling path, allowing the received socket buffer to be freed before returning the error code and preventing a resource leak.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an error cleanup path in `ncsi_rcv_rsp()` to free `skb` before returning and prevent skb leaks on failure.
intent_record.what: A new error-handling label `err_free_skb:` was added at the end of `ncsi_rcv_rsp()`, which calls `kfree_skb(skb);` and then returns `ret`.
intent_record.how: This introduces a cleanup path that explicitly frees the received socket buffer before returning on error paths that jump to `err_free_skb`, preventing the skb from being left allocated and avoiding a memory leak during response handling failures.

grouping_result.intent: Add an error cleanup path in `ncsi_rcv_rsp()` to free `skb` before returning and prevent skb leaks on failure.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure all early error returns in ncsi_rcv_rsp() flow through a common cleanup path that frees skb and avoids buffer leaks.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly target the root cause by converting early error returns in ncsi_rcv_rsp() into a common cleanup path that frees the received skb on validation/lookup failures, preventing the buffer leaks described.

candidates.rationale: This early return in ncsi_aen_handler() exits on invalid AEN lookup failure without going through a cleanup path, matching the root cause of not freeing the received skb on error.
This early return in ncsi_rcv_rsp() for missing device bypasses the common exit path, so the received skb is not freed.
This unrecognized-packet error return in ncsi_rcv_rsp() directly exits instead of flowing through cleanup, causing skb ownership to be mishandled and leaked.
This early return on an unused request exits after unlocking but before any skb cleanup, directly embodying the leak-causing error path.

vuln_statements.explanation: In ncsi_rcv_rsp(), this direct error return on the missing-device path exits before the common cleanup path that frees the received sk_buff, causing the skb ownership leak described in the root cause.
In ncsi_rcv_rsp(), this early return for an unrecognized packet bypasses the shared exit/cleanup handling, so the received sk_buff is not freed on this validation failure.
In ncsi_aen_handler(), this direct return on invalid AEN lookup failure skips the common exit block responsible for cleanup/finalization, leaving the received sk_buff unfreed.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet includes the full body of `ncsi_rcv_rsp()`, which is the relevant receive-path function, so it is sufficient to judge ownership handling. The root cause is missing `sk_buff` free on validation/lookup failures. In this version, several error paths return or exit without any visible skb free. First, early lookup failures return directly: `if (!ndp) return -ENODEV;` and later `if (!nrh) { ... return -ENOENT; }`. More importantly for the request-associated receive path, after `nr->rsp = skb;`, the function can fail on `if (!nr->used) { ... return -ENODEV; }`, `if (!nr->enabled) { ... ret = -ENOENT; goto out; }`, and `ret = ncsi_validate_rsp_pkt(nr, payload); if (ret) goto out;`. The `out:` path only does `ncsi_free_request(nr); return ret;` and does not explicitly free `skb`. There is no visible corrective handling such as `dev_kfree_skb(skb)`/`consume_skb(skb)` on these failure paths. Since this commit introduces the response handler with these error exits and no skb release logic shown, the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet includes the full body of `ncsi_rcv_rsp()`, which is the relevant receive-path function, so it is sufficient. The vulnerable construct is present because the function takes ownership of the received `skb` via `nr->rsp = skb;` but has early return paths before that skb is associated/freed correctly. In particular: (1) if no NCSI device is found, `if (!ndp) return -ENODEV;` returns directly with no `kfree_skb()` or similar; (2) if no handler is found, `if (!nrh) { ... return -ENOENT; }` also returns directly without freeing `skb`; (3) after request lookup, `if (!nr->used) { spin_unlock_irqrestore(&ndp->lock, flags); return -ENODEV; }` again returns directly without freeing `skb`. These are exactly validation/lookup failure style exits in the receive path that leak the received `sk_buff`. Although later error paths go through `goto out; ... ncsi_free_request(nr);`, the direct returns above show the vulnerable ownership handling. No explicit skb free is present on those direct error returns, so the fix is not present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it shows the full receive-path handler and its skb cleanup behavior. The stated root cause is returning from ncsi_aen_handler() on validation/lookup failures without freeing the received sk_buff. In this snippet, skb freeing is handled centrally via the common exit path: after validation and handler dispatch, execution reaches `out:` and calls `consume_skb(skb);` before `return ret;`. Validation failure uses `if (ret) goto out;`, so the skb is freed on that error path as well. For unsupported AEN types, the code does `if (!nah) { ... return -ENOENT; }`, which is a direct return without `consume_skb(skb)`. However, the root cause described specifically concerns validation/lookup failures in `ncsi_aen_handler()` and `ncsi_rcv_rsp()`. The handler lookup within `ncsi_aen_handler()` for the AEN type is present, but the packet/channel lookup failures inside subhandlers such as `ncsi_aen_handler_lsc()` (`if (!nc) return -ENODEV;`) still propagate back to `ncsi_aen_handler()`, which then reaches `out:` and frees the skb. Thus the vulnerable construct described—returning on validation or channel lookup failure without freeing skb—is not present here. The code already contains the fix pattern for those paths via the `goto out` / `consume_skb(skb)` cleanup.
